clownfish.definition: A small tropical saltwater fish that shelters among sea anemones and is a popular choice for home aquariums.
clownfish.exampleUsage: The clownfish was identified during the lesson.

angelfish.definition: Sharks with broad flat bodies and winglike pectoral fins but that swim the way sharks do.

parrotfish.definition: Gaudy tropical fishes with parrotlike beaks formed by fusion of teeth.
parrotfish.exampleUsage: The parrotfish was identified during the lesson.

pufferfish.definition: Any of numerous marine fishes whose elongated spiny body can inflate itself with water or air to form a globe.
pufferfish.exampleUsage: The pufferfish was identified during the lesson.

lionfish.definition: Brightly striped fish of the tropical Pacific having elongated spiny fins.
lionfish.exampleUsage: The lionfish was identified during the lesson.

surgeonfish.definition: Brightly colored coral-reef fish with knifelike spines at the tail.
surgeonfish.exampleUsage: The surgeonfish was identified during the lesson.

butterflyfish.definition: Tropical fish with huge fanlike pectoral fins for underwater gliding.
butterflyfish.exampleUsage: The butterflyfish was identified during the lesson.

grouper.definition: Usually solitary bottom sea basses of warm seas.

moray-eel.definition: A long, snake-like marine fish that often hides in holes and crevices in tropical or subtropical reefs.
moray-eel.exampleUsage: A moray eel looked out from a rocky crevice.

barracuda.definition: Any voracious marine fish of the genus Sphyraena having an elongated cylindrical body and large mouth with projecting lower jaw and long strong teeth.
barracuda.exampleUsage: The barracuda was identified during the lesson.

seahorse.definition: Either of two large northern marine mammals having ivory tusks and tough hide over thick blubber.
seahorse.exampleUsage: The seahorse was identified during the lesson.

triggerfish.definition: Any of numerous compressed deep-bodied tropical fishes with sandpapery skin and erectile spines in the first dorsal fin.
triggerfish.exampleUsage: The triggerfish was identified during the lesson.

dolphin.definition: Large slender food and game fish widely distributed in warm seas (especially around Hawaii).
dolphin.exampleUsage: The dolphin was identified during the lesson.

sea-turtle.definition: Large turtles that spend most of their lives in tropical or subtropical oceans come ashore mainly to lay eggs on sandy beaches.
sea-turtle.arabicTranslation: كائن أو عنصر طبيعي يُسمّى «سيا تورتلي»

manatee.definition: Sirenian mammal of tropical coastal waters of America.
manatee.exampleUsage: The manatee was identified during the lesson.

whale-shark.definition: The world's largest living fish, a gentle filter-feeding shark with a broad head and spotted body.
whale-shark.exampleUsage: A whale shark swam slowly through the open water.

manta-ray.definition: A very large ray with broad triangular fins that feeds mainly on tiny organisms filtered from the water.
manta-ray.exampleUsage: The manta ray glided above the reef.

stingray.definition: Large venomous ray with large barbed spines near the base of a thin whiplike tail capable of inflicting severe wounds.

sea-snake.definition: A snake adapted to marine life, found mainly in warm coastal waters.
sea-snake.exampleUsage: The guide observed a sea snake from a safe distance.

dugong.definition: Sirenian tusked mammal found from eastern Africa to Australia.
dugong.exampleUsage: The dugong was identified during the lesson.

humpback-whale.definition: A large baleen whale known for long pectoral fins and complex songs.
humpback-whale.exampleUsage: A humpback whale surfaced beyond the reef.

otter.definition: A swimming mammal with thick fur and a long body that lives near water.

coral.definition: The hard stony skeleton of a Mediterranean coral that has a delicate red or pink color and is used for jewelry.

sea-anemone.definition: A stationary marine cnidarian, or stinging sea animal, is a predator with a cylindrical body and tentacles around its central mouth, usually anchored to a surface by a basal disc.
sea-anemone.exampleUsage: The sea anemone was identified during the lesson.

starfish.definition: Echinoderms characterized by five arms extending from a central disk.

sea-urchin.definition: A small round marine animal with a hard shell covered in movable spines.
sea-urchin.exampleUsage: A sea urchin rested between the rocks.

jellyfish.definition: Any of numerous usually marine and free-swimming coelenterates that constitute the sexually reproductive forms of hydrozoans and scyphozoans.

octopus.definition: Tentacles of octopus prepared as food.

crab.definition: A stroke of the oar that either misses the water or digs too deeply.

lobster.definition: A large sea animal with a hard shell and two strong claws.

shrimp.definition: Small slender-bodied chiefly marine decapod crustaceans with a long tail and single pair of pincers.

sea-cucumber.definition: A soft, elongated marine animal related to starfish and sea urchins, usually living on the seabed.
sea-cucumber.exampleUsage: A sea cucumber moved slowly across the sandy bottom.

coral-reef.definition: A rigid calcium carbonate framework, built from coral skeletons, provides the reef with its physical structure.

seagrass.definition: Any of various seaweeds that grow underwater in shallow beds.

kelp.definition: Large brown seaweeds having fluted leathery fronds.

algae.definition: Primitive chlorophyll-containing mainly aquatic eukaryotic organisms lacking true stems and roots and leaves.

tide-pool.definition: A small pool of seawater left among rocks when the tide goes out.
tide-pool.exampleUsage: Small crabs were visible in the tide pool.

lagoon.definition: A body of water cut off from a larger body by a reef of sand or coral.

sand-bar.definition: A ridge of sand that builds up in a river, lake, or coastal water.

underwater-cave.definition: A natural hollow or passage beneath the surface of the water.
underwater-cave.exampleUsage: Researchers mapped the entrance to an underwater cave.

rock-formation.definition: The natural creation of rock inside Earth’s crust occurs when melted material cools, sediments harden, or existing rock changes under heat and pressure.

current.definition: A steady flow of a fluid (usually from natural causes).

snorkel.definition: Breathing device consisting of a bent tube fitting into a swimmer's mouth and extending above the surface.
snorkel.exampleUsage: The snorkel was used during the activity.

diving-mask.definition: A watertight mask that covers the eyes and nose so a diver can see underwater.
diving-mask.exampleUsage: The diver checked that the diving mask fitted securely.

fins.definition: To show the fins above the water while swimming.

wetsuit.definition: A close-fitting suit made from insulating material and worn in water to reduce heat loss and protect the skin.
wetsuit.exampleUsage: The researcher wore a wetsuit in the cool water.

oxygen-tank.definition: A strong cylinder designed to store oxygen gas; diving systems more commonly use tanks of compressed breathing gas rather than pure oxygen.
oxygen-tank.exampleUsage: The safety lesson distinguishes oxygen tanks from ordinary compressed-air scuba cylinders.

regulator.definition: Any of various controls or devices for regulating or controlling fluid flow, pressure, temperature, etc.
regulator.exampleUsage: The regulator was used during the activity.

dive-computer.definition: An electronic device worn by a diver that tracks information such as depth and time to support safer dive planning.
dive-computer.exampleUsage: The dive computer recorded depth and elapsed time.

underwater-camera.definition: A camera designed or protected so it can take photographs or video while submerged.
underwater-camera.exampleUsage: The underwater camera recorded coral and fish.

weight-belt.definition: A belt that carries weights to help a diver control buoyancy underwater.
weight-belt.exampleUsage: The training display shows a weight belt as part of diving equipment.

dive-flag.definition: A flag used to warn boaters that divers are in the water nearby.
dive-flag.exampleUsage: The dive flag warned nearby boats that divers were below.

marine-reserve.definition: A protected sea area where human activities are restricted to conserve habitats and wildlife.
marine-reserve.exampleUsage: Fishing is restricted in the marine reserve.

coral-bleaching.definition: The loss of color in corals can damage reef habitats and reduce the variety of species they support.

pollution.definition: Undesirable state of the natural environment being contaminated with harmful substances as a consequence of human activities.

plastic-waste.definition: Discarded plastic material that can pollute land, rivers, and oceans.
plastic-waste.exampleUsage: Volunteers removed plastic waste from the shoreline.

fishing-net.definition: A tangled mass of fishing netting is treated as something to manage, repair, or discard rather than as an active tool.
fishing-net.exampleUsage: The fishing net was identified during the lesson.

conservation-sign.definition: A sign that gives rules or information intended to protect wildlife, habitats, or natural resources.
conservation-sign.exampleUsage: The conservation sign asked visitors not to touch the coral.

research-boat.definition: A vessel equipped or used for scientific study on the water.
research-boat.exampleUsage: The research boat carried marine biologists to the reef.

water-sample.definition: Water collected from a particular source is examined to identify its contents and condition.

reef-restoration.definition: Work intended to repair damaged reef habitat or help coral communities recover.
reef-restoration.exampleUsage: The project uses reef restoration to support damaged coral areas.

aquarium.definition: A tank or pool or bowl filled with water for keeping live fish and underwater animals.
aquarium.exampleUsage: The aquarium was identified during the lesson.

brain-coral.definition: A type of hard coral whose grooved surface often resembles the folds of a brain.
brain-coral.exampleUsage: Brain coral formed rounded shapes on the reef.

fan-coral.definition: A branching soft coral or sea fan that grows in a flat, fan-like shape.
fan-coral.exampleUsage: A large fan coral moved gently in the current.

staghorn-coral.definition: Describing coral with branches that resemble the antlers of a male deer.
staghorn-coral.arabicTranslation: كائن أو عنصر طبيعي يُسمّى «ستاغورن كورال»

tube-coral.definition: A coral form made of tube-shaped structures or polyps.
tube-coral.exampleUsage: Tube coral grew on a shaded part of the reef.

fire-coral.definition: A colonial marine organism related to hydrozoans that resembles coral and can cause a painful sting when touched.
fire-coral.exampleUsage: The guide warned visitors not to touch fire coral.

mushroom-coral.definition: A coral with a broad disc-like or mushroom-shaped body, often living as an individual rather than a fixed colony.
mushroom-coral.exampleUsage: A mushroom coral rested on the reef surface.

table-coral.definition: A branching hard coral that grows outward in a broad, table-like shape.
table-coral.exampleUsage: Table coral created a wide shelter for small fish.

soft-coral.definition: A coral without a massive hard limestone skeleton, often flexible and able to sway with currents.
soft-coral.exampleUsage: Soft coral moved gently with the water.

reef-wall.definition: A steep underwater face or slope formed by a coral reef.
reef-wall.exampleUsage: Divers observed the reef wall from a safe distance.

anemone.definition: Any woodland plant of the genus Anemone grown for its beautiful flowers and whorls of dissected leaves.

sandy-bottom.definition: An area of the seabed mainly covered with sand.
sandy-bottom.exampleUsage: A ray rested on the sandy bottom beside the reef.
